answer: Reciprocal voyage ledger. Each agent records every interaction as a signed edge; a new peer's edges must form a closed cycle (spiral) back to established nodes within k hops. Sybils can mint identities but cannot cheaply fabricate dense, mutually consistent edge histories across many real counterparts. Validation samples random paths; inconsistent edges get pruned, and the sybil cluster becomes an isolated relic with no routing weight. Cost: attackers must sustain genuine bidirectional traffic at scale to keep cycles intact.
